title: Sustainable membrane‐integrated technologies for tannery wastewater treatment toward membrane innovations, fouling control, and techno‐economic scalability
content:
Abstract

Tannery wastewater is one of the most complex industrial effluents, which requires multiple stages of treatment due to its pollutant contents such as chromium (10–1000 mg/L), COD (7000–24,000 mg/L), TDS (3800–23,000 mg/L), and azo dyes (80–440 mg/L). This review critically analyses different membrane technologies for treating tannery wastewater generated during pre-tanning, tanning, and post-tanning operations, which include membrane modification mechanisms and permeate flux per unit pressure vs. energy trade-offs toward industrial application potential. NF membranes achieve 90–95% chromium recovery and 85–95% sulfate rejection at 4–30 bar, enabling reuse of recovered chromium sulfate and reducing fresh chemical consumption by up to 40%. Integrated UF-NF-RO trains attain 95–99% COD removal at specific energy consumption of 1.5–6.0 kWh/m3, compared to 2–3 kWh/m3 for standalone MBR systems and 3–5 kWh/m3 for FO-MD hybrids. Surface-modified membranes reduce irreversible fouling by 30–60% and extend membrane service intervals by 25–40% compared with unmodified membranes. Techno-economic analysis shows that membrane-based chromium recovery reduces total treatment capital costs by 34% compared with conventional physicochemical systems at the 200 m3/day scale, with payback periods of 3–5 years. Critical limitations are identified: NF and RO flux declines by 30–50% within 72 h under real tannery feed variability; irreversible chromium-organic scaling causes permanent 20–35% flux loss; and AI/IoT fouling prediction systems remain at industrial readiness levels 4–5 with unresolved model transferability challenges. The review identifies key research priorities: standardized long-term performance testing under real tannery matrices, low-cost robust ceramic membrane development, and validated techno-economic frameworks for ZLD deployment in developing-nation tanneries.
